items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-12-30
items.q: Judge Sanders, he's dead, passed a decision. He told him, he says, when you police once go out to this man's place...

ctx.x: That's right. Did you have any kind of trouble with the law?

No trouble until after we had operated around and I had gotten all of the business in town, the other clubs were suffering. And the white operators got together themselves. They did everything they could to get the policemen to close the place. And, of course, the liquor control laws in those days had gotten to the place where at 12 o'clock at night you'd have to stop operating and stop drinking. But I was able to operate in our club until 2, 3 o'clock in the morning, not serving any drinks and not having any…
You know, I keep thinking that while I'm here, part of what I want to do is get to the libraries and see some of those old newspapers, you know, if you knew the date.
